comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh2026–2027 BA-ENG and39 actual module responses reverify the nine first-year and eleven selected second-year components:60+60=120 unique EC. Independent Literature3/4 choices retain first-listed British options and Philology4 retains first-listed Early Modern Everyday English. The four academic learning pathways are not formal degree specialisations: current OER2.2 says not applicable. Appendix F confirms2025/2026 substitutions but contains no revised BA3 allocation. Current BA3 explicitly changes significantly from2027–2028; Language Acquisition5/6 are last offered2026–2027 and are excluded from the entrant pathway. The current outgoing pattern of30 EC open space,10 EC specialisation,10 EC language acquisition and10 EC thesis is recorded internally, not certified for2026 entrants. Forward-year2271 request returns2261 unchanged. Current thesis is10 EC,7500–10000 words; mandatory seminar0 EC, mentoring0 EC. OER4.2 requires130 earned programme EC for thesis entry, controlling over module wording that permits nearing130. Formal old-code linguistic prerequisites require actual transition equivalences, not presumed code identity. Current public pages and2027–2028 brochure clarify academic substance but do not publish the revised final60EC. The accreditation report describes the older pathway and planned block minor, not adopted replacements. Preserve all valid first120EC, contemporary text/AI and historical-language evidence; no current-cohort replacement credits invented.

audience.programmeDescription: English Language and Culture at Leiden combines literary study, linguistics, English language development and philology. Students analyse literature from different periods and English-speaking cultures, study the structure and historical development of English, and practise academic writing and speaking. Philology includes reading older English texts, examining manuscripts and using digital corpora. Contemporary work also considers how genre, context and AI affect writing.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first two years are shown below. The revised final-year requirements still need confirmation before a complete UCR comparison can be made. The unresolved curriculum does not establish that UCR offers no relevant study possibilities.

curriculum.routeLabel: First two years: British literature and Early Modern English choices
curriculum.limitation: The table covers 120 EC from the first two years. The programme’s final year is being revised, and its applicable requirements are not yet confirmed. These components do not constitute a complete degree pathway.

componentNotes.y1-5621vel1y: Develops spoken English through pronunciation, vocabulary and presentations, while examining international varieties and their social meanings.
componentNotes.y1-5621vfimey: Students read and translate parts of Chaucer in Middle English and study elementary grammar and medieval cultural contexts.
componentNotes.y1-5621villy: Examines intertextual and cultural exchange between Italian and English literature, ideas and media.
componentNotes.y1-5621vel2y: Develops academic and professional writing, including research, source evaluation, argument and writing for different audiences.
componentNotes.y1-5621vlg2y: Introduces the analysis of English sounds and sentence structure.
componentNotes.y1-5621vpoey: Combines Old English grammar and translation with the interpretation of early medieval prose and poetry.
componentNotes.y2-5000vhdw1y: Introduces digital humanities through media, AI and data, with practical research-tool assignments.
componentNotes.y2-5622vel3y: Studies grammar and stylistic choices as tools for accurate and effective writing.
componentNotes.y2-5622vlg3y: Develops syntactic analysis and studies variation in English sounds, including practical phonetic analysis with PRAAT.
componentNotes.y2-5622vel4y: Studies register, genre and style, including comparisons between human-composed and AI-generated texts.
componentNotes.y2-5622vli4y: Develops generative analyses of English syntax and the suprasegmental structure of speech.
componentNotes.y2-5622kbly: The British option is selected for this semester. The American option remains an alternative, and the next semester’s choice is independent.
componentNotes.y2-5622kl4bny: The British option is selected independently for this semester. It surveys nineteenth-century fiction in its cultural and historical contexts.
componentNotes.y2-5622kfe1my: The selected Philology option studies everyday Early Modern English through varied records, manuscript transcription and corpus tools. Medieval English literature is the alternative option.
